title_zh: 池州南泉普願禪師語錄
title_en: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Nanquan Puyuan
cbeta_id: X1315 (古尊宿語錄·池州南泉普願禪師語要)
author_zh: 唐 池州 南泉普願 禪師 說 (馬祖法嗣)
author_en: Chan Master Nanquan Puyuan (748–835 CE), Teacher of Zhaozhou Congshen
genre: Discourse Record & Radical Encounters (語錄與機鋒)
overview: The sharp, enigmatic, and revolutionary encounters of Master Nanquan Puyuan, teacher of Zhaozhou, famed for 'Ordinary Mind is the Way' (平常心是道), cutting the cat in two (斬貓), and becoming a water buffalo (水牯牛).

sections.title_zh: 百年後作水牯牛：銜取一莖草來
sections.title_pinyin: Bǎinián Hòu Zuò Shuǐgǔniú: Xián Qǔ Yī Jīng Cǎo Lái
sections.title_en: Reborn as a Water Buffalo: Bring a Blade of Grass

dialogue.speaker: Monk / 僧
dialogue.zh: 師遷化前，僧問：「和尚百年後，向甚處去？」
dialogue.pinyin: Shī qiānhuà qián, sēng wèn: 'Héshang bǎinián hòu, xiàng shèn chù qù?'

red_pine.text: Before the Master passed away, a monk asked: 'After you pass on, Master, where will you go?'

cleary.text: Before the Master's passing, a monk asked, 'After a hundred years, where will the Master go?'

sasaki.text: Before Nansen passed away, a monk asked: 'After your death, Master, where will you go?'

dialogue.speaker: Nanquan / 南泉
dialogue.zh: 師曰：「山下作一頭水牯牛去。」僧曰：「學人隨和尚去得否？」師曰：「汝若隨我，銜取一莖草來。」
dialogue.pinyin: Shī yuē: 'Shānxià zuò yī tóu shuǐgǔniú qù.' Sēng yuē: 'Xuérén suí héshang qù dé fǒu?' Shī yuē: 'Rǔ ruò suí wǒ, xián qǔ yī jīng cǎo lái.'

red_pine.text: The Master said: 'I will go down to the foot of the mountain and become a water buffalo.' The monk said: 'May I follow you there, Master?' The Master said: 'If you wish to follow me, you must bring a blade of grass in your mouth!'

cleary.text: The Master said, 'I will go to the foot of the mountain and become a water buffalo.' The monk said, 'May I follow the Master?' The Master said, 'If you follow me, bring a blade of grass in your mouth.'

sasaki.text: Nansen said: 'I will go down the mountain and be a water buffalo.' The monk said: 'May I follow you?' Nansen said: 'If you follow me, you must come with a mouthful of grass!'

sections.title_pinyin: Bù Shì Xīn, Bù Shì Fó, Bù Shì Wù
sections.title_en: It is Not Mind, Not Buddha, Not a Thing

dialogue.speaker: Monk / 僧
dialogue.zh: 僧問：「古人生生世世，說心說佛。和尚今日說何法？」
dialogue.pinyin: Sēng wèn: 'Gǔrén shēngshēng shìshì, shuō xīn shuō fó. Héshang jīnrì shuō hé fǎ?'

red_pine.text: A monk asked: 'Generation after generation the ancients spoke of Mind and spoke of Buddha. What Dharma do you teach today, Master?'

cleary.text: A monk asked, 'The ancients for generations spoke of mind and Buddha. What teaching does the Master preach today?'

sasaki.text: A monk asked: 'Ancient masters always preached mind and preached Buddha. What do you teach today?'

dialogue.speaker: Nanquan / 南泉
dialogue.zh: 師曰：「不是心，不是佛，不是物。」僧曰：「向甚處歸著？」師曰：「任汝穿耳，任汝踏毛。」
dialogue.pinyin: Shī yuē: 'Bù shì xīn, bù shì fó, bù shì wù.' Sēng yuē: 'Xiàng shèn chù guīzhuó?' Shī yuē: 'Rèn rǔ chuān'ěr, rèn rǔ tàmáo.'

red_pine.text: The Master said: 'It is not mind, it is not Buddha, it is not a thing.' The monk said: 'Where does one rest then?' The Master said: 'Pierce your ears as you please, trample your fur as you wish!'

cleary.text: The Master said, 'Not mind, not Buddha, not a thing.' The monk said, 'Where does it belong?' The Master said, 'Let your ears be pierced, let your hair be trodden.'

sasaki.text: Nansen said: 'Not mind, not Buddha, not a thing.' The monk said: 'Where does one settle?' Nansen said: 'Pierce your ears and tread on your fur!'

sections.title_zh: 陸亘大夫看牡丹：如夢相似
sections.title_pinyin: Lù Gèn Dàfū Kàn Mǔdān: Rú Mèng Xiàngsì
sections.title_en: Governor Lu Gen and the Peony Flower: Like a Dream

dialogue.speaker: Governor Lu / 陸亘大夫
dialogue.zh: 陸亘大夫問南泉：「肇法師道：『天地與我同根，萬物與我一體。』也甚奇怪。」
dialogue.pinyin: Lù Gèn dàfū wèn Nánquán: 'Zhào fǎshī dào: 'Tiāndì yǔ wǒ tóng gēn, wànwù yǔ wǒ yītǐ.' Yě shèn qīguài.'

red_pine.text: Governor Lu Gen asked Nanquan: 'Master Sengzhao said: Heaven and earth share the same root with me; the myriad things are one body with me. Isn't this truly extraordinary?'

cleary.text: Governor Lu Gen asked Nanquan, 'Master Sengzhao said, Heaven and earth share the same root with me, the myriad things are of one body with me. Isn't this most extraordinary?'

sasaki.text: Governor Riko said to Nansen: 'Master Jō said: Heaven and earth share the same root as myself; all things are one with me. Isn't this wondrous?'

dialogue.speaker: Nanquan / 南泉
dialogue.zh: 南泉指庭前牡丹花曰：「大夫！時人見此一株花，如夢相似。」大夫罔措。
dialogue.pinyin: Nánquán zhǐ tíng qián mǔdān huā yuē: 'Dàfū! Shí rén jiàn cǐ yī zhū huā, rú mèng xiàngsì.' Dàfū wǎngcuò.

red_pine.text: Nanquan pointed to a blooming peony in the courtyard and said: 'Governor! People of the world look at this single flower as if in a dream!' The Governor was at a loss.

cleary.text: Nanquan pointed to a peony in the garden: 'Governor, people today see this flower as if in a dream.' The Governor was nonplussed.

sasaki.text: Nansen pointed to a peony flower in the garden: 'Governor, people of this world look at this flower as if in a dream.' Riko was speechless.
